members.name: close
members.summary: Closes the underlying file, no matter what.

members.name: close_intelligently
members.summary: This function only closes the file if it was opened by the lazy file wrapper.  For instance this will never close stdin.

members.name: open
members.summary: Opens the file if it's not yet open.  This call might fail with a `FileError`.  Not handling this error will produce an error that Click shows.

items.name: LazyFile
items.summary: A lazy file works like a regular file but it does not fully open the file but it does perform some basic checks early to see if the filename parameter does make sense.  This is useful for safely opening files for writing.

items.name: PacifyFlushWrapper
items.summary: This wrapper is used to catch and suppress BrokenPipeErrors resulting from ``.flush()`` being called on broken pipe during the shutdown/final-GC of the Python interpreter. Notably ``.flush()`` is always called on ``sys.stdout`` and ``sys.s…

items.name: _detect_program_name
items.signature: def _detect_program_name(path: str | None = None, _main: ModuleType | None = None) -> str
items.summary: Determine the command used to run the program, for use in help text. If a file or entry point was executed, the file name is returned. If ``python -m`` was used to execute a module or package, ``python -m name`` is returned.

items.name: _expand_args
items.signature: def _expand_args(args: Iterable[str], user: bool = True, env: bool = True, glob_recursive: bool = True) -> list[str]
items.summary: Simulate Unix shell expansion with Python functions.

items.name: echo
items.signature: def echo(message: Any | None = None, file: IO[Any] | None = None, nl: bool = True, err: bool = False, color: bool | None = None) -> None
items.summary: Print a message and newline to stdout or a file. This should be used instead of `print` because it provides better support for different data, files, and environments.

items.name: format_filename
items.signature: def format_filename(filename: str | bytes | os.PathLike[str] | os.PathLike[bytes], shorten: bool = False) -> str
items.summary: Format a filename as a string for display. Ensures the filename can be displayed by replacing any invalid bytes or surrogate escapes in the name with the replacement character ``�``.

items.name: get_app_dir
items.signature: def get_app_dir(app_name: str, roaming: bool = True, force_posix: bool = False) -> str
items.summary: Returns the config folder for the application.  The default behavior is to return whatever is most appropriate for the operating system.

items.name: get_binary_stream
items.summary: Returns a system stream for byte processing.

items.name: get_text_stream
items.signature: def get_text_stream(name: Literal['stdin', 'stdout', 'stderr'], encoding: str | None = None, errors: str | None = 'strict') -> TextIO
items.summary: Returns a system stream for text processing.  This usually returns a wrapped stream around a binary stream returned from `get_binary_stream` but it also can take shortcuts for already correctly configured streams.

items.name: make_default_short_help
items.signature: def make_default_short_help(help: str, max_length: int = 45) -> str
items.summary: Returns a condensed version of help string.

items.name: safecall
items.signature: def safecall(func: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, R | None]
items.summary: Wraps a function so that it swallows exceptions.
